SIE EXAM STUDY GUIDE

How to study Products and Risks for the SIE exam

Products and Risks is 44% of the SIE, so it is usually the best place to spend extra study time. Learn each product by comparing its features, investor fit, tax treatment, liquidity and risk. Then practice choosing between similar concepts in question form.

Reviewed 2026-09-04. Based on FINRA's published SIE format and content outline.

Study comparisons instead of isolated definitions

A definition alone is rarely enough. Put securities side by side: common stock and preferred stock, open-end funds and closed-end funds, bonds and bond funds. Ask what changes when rates move, who carries risk, and how an investor can sell.

Turn recurring errors into a short list

If you repeatedly confuse a rule or product feature, write one plain-language note and revisit it before your next set. Avoid collecting a huge notebook of copied definitions. A small list of your own errors is more useful because it reflects the mistakes you actually make.

Ask for the missing distinction

After an error, a helpful question is often narrower than 'why is this wrong?'. Ask what fact separates the correct choice from the closest distractor. Bona Fide's tutor has the question and your selected choice in context, so you can follow the explanation with that exact distinction.

Keep the official outline nearby

FINRA's content outline is the authoritative source for what can be tested. Use this guide to organize your study, then check the original whenever you need the exact wording or current exam information.
